description: Proposed amendments [in conjunction with NMA Application reference 2025/3642] to convert 1-6 Church Row back to separate single townhouses with access to amenity spaces to the rear, minor amendments to 7-9 Church Row to provide each home with its own entrance, two lightweight glass box extensions to rear of houses to provide suitable entrances, minor amendment to mews to rear to accommodate change and optimisation of new build to add horizontal link at fourth floor and add bolt on balconies.

Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall be begun within 3 years from the date of this permission.
Reason: To prevent the accumulation of unimplemented planning permissions and to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended) and to meet the requirements of Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004 and to meet the requirements of The Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) (England) Order 2015.
Condition : 2 - 2.In accordance with drawings
The development shall be carried out in accordance with the reports, specifications and drawings detailed below:

Documents: 
- Cover Letter dated 18/09/2025, prepared by St George, titled: TOWN AND COUNTRY PLANNING ACT 1990 (AS AMENDED), Phase 3 1-9 Church Row, Wandsworth Plain, SW18 1ES. APPLICATION FOR LISTED BUILDING CONSENT FOR AMENDMENTS TO THE CONSENTED SCHEME REF 2012/1847 dated 1st December 2017. 
- Heritage Impact Assessment; address: Ram Terraces- Phase 3, 1-9 Church Row Wandsworth London SW18; prepared by: Steven Levrant Heritage Architecture Ltd; reference: M047-HER11-B3B-ZZ-RP-A-880-001 Rev-P02; dated: September 2025. 
- Design and Access Statement: address: 1-9 Church Row Phase 3 Wandsworth Mills London SW18; prepared by: DGA Architects; reference: M047-DAV12-P3-XX-DSH-A-045-005 Rev P07; dated: September 2025

Reason: To ensure a satisfactory standard of development and to allow the Local Planning Authority to review any potential changes to the scheme. 
Condition : 3 - Details of Pre-construction External Repairs
Prior to commencement of each relevant building between Numbers 1 to 9 Church Row, details of the following shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with Historic England. 
a)	Method of protection of historic features externally during building works
b)	Any methods to be used to clean the external fabric of the buildings, including but not limited to brick cleaning method.
c)	Methods of repointing/brick repair if any required including mortar sample. 
d)	Pointing schedule, all repointing should be done in lime to an appropriate historic appearance.
e)	Feasibility of reusing removed historic windows elsewhere. 
f)	Window schedule itemising any windows to be repaired and/or replaced with justification for their replacement and proposed design.
g)	Door schedule itemising any doors to be repaired and /or replaced with justification for their replacement and proposed design. 
a)	Construction work to the listed buildings including, but not limited to: 
i)	Repairs to existing roof. 
ii)	Samples of replacement tile where applicable. 
iii)	External finishes including paint finishes
iv)	Structural and repair works
v)	treatment of external historic fixtures.
The works shall be implements in accordance with the approved details.

Reason: To ensure the preservation of the special interest of the building affected by the works hereby approved, in accordance with policy LP3 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 4 - Details of New Works
A - Prior to commencement of each relevant building between Numbers 1 to 9 Church Row, details of the following shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with Historic England, excluding repair work listed in Condition 3. 
a)	The proposed glazed boxes, including but not limited to the following: 
i)	their method of attachment to the existing building, 
ii)	how will the joins be detailed,
iii)	framing of the boxes 
iv)	measures to avoid internal light spill at night. 
b)	The external finish around the access-way through numbers 7-9. 
c)	Proposed service runs. These should be concealed and when the historic fabric would have to be removed it should be made good / replaced using like for like materials and techniques to best conservation practice. Existing appropriate service ducts should be re-used;
d)	Inventory of all proposed internal and external light fittings
e)	Inventory of all internal fire/smoke alarms. 
f)	Windows' schedule itemising new additions and proposed design
g)	Doors' schedule itemising new additions and proposed design (including the doors to the front lightwell).
h)	New Rooftops, including but not limited to 
i)	external materials for the terraces,
ii)	rooftop coverings,
i)	Construction and demolition work to the listed buildings including, but not limited to: 
vi)	internal partitions 
vii)	new floors
viii)	new mezzanine floors
ix)	internal demolition to existing buildings
x)	removal and alterations to fixtures and fittings
xi)	details of all proposed internal joinery and mouldings at a scale of 1:5 for mouldings and 1:20 for joinery
xii)	details of ceiling if there are replacements proposed. These should be of traditional timber lath and plaster construction or to match existing
xiii)	internal and external finishes
xiv)	structural and repair works, and
xv)	treatment of historic fixtures.
The works shall be implements in accordance with the approved 
Condition : 5 - Details of landscaping
Prior to commencement of each phase, details of the following shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with Historic England, excluding repair work listed in Condition 3:
a)	Hard/soft landscaping for the listed building (Phase 3A) 
b)	Hard and soft landscaping for new building (Phase 3B)
The works shall be implements in accordance with the approved details.

Reason: T in accordance with policy LP3 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.

Reason: To ensure the preservation of the special interest of the building affected by the works hereby approved and  ensure a satisfactory appearance, provide tree planting and biodiversity improvements, in accordance with Council policies LP1, LP2, LP3 and LP56 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework. The details are required prior to the commencement of works to ensure the landscaping measures are incorporated in the layout and construction of the development.
Condition : 6 - Details relevant to Phase 3b
Prior to commencement of the relevant phase, details of the following shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, excluding repair work listed in Condition 3. 
a)	Details of external materials and detailing for new building
b)	Details of balcony balustrade treatment for new building

The works shall be implements in accordance with the approved details.

Reason: To ensure the preservation of the special interest of the building affected by the works hereby approved, in accordance with policy LP2, LP3 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 7 - Photographic Evidence
Prior to commencement of any building works to Numbers 1 to 9 Church Row, photographic recordings of the buildings externally and internally to be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The approved record shall be deposited with Historic England and Local History Library. 

Reason: To ensure the preservation of the special interest of the building affected by the works hereby approved, in accordance with policy LP3 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 8 - Details of Basement Works 
Prior to commencement of each relevant building between Numbers 1 to 9 Church Row, details of the following shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with Historic England, excluding repair work listed in Condition 3. 
h)	Method of protection of historic features internally during building works
i)	Flood prevention methods, their appearance and fitting within the building fabric. 
j)	Any damp-proofing/lining required to the basement areas, its appearance and fitting within the building fabric.  
k)	Any underpinning and lowering of floor level in the basement areas, its impact on the fabric of the building and significance of surviving features including but not limited to surviving fireplaces.

The works shall be implements in accordance with the approved details.

Reason: To ensure the preservation of the special interest of the building affected by the works hereby approved and to ensure a high quality development, in accordance with policies LP1, LP2, LP3 and LP4 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework
Condition : 9 - 9.Archaeology (Condition 3)
A.	The development shall not be occupied until the site investigation and post-investigation assessment has been completed in accordance with the programme set out in the Written Scheme of Investigation approved under Planning Permissions 2022/2086 and 2023/0603), and the provision for analysis, publication and dissemination of the results and archive deposition has been secured.
B.	A copy of the recording taken shall be provided to the Local Planning Authority's Conservation and Design team and local history library.

Reason: To secure appropriate historical records of the site and publication of results, in accordance with Section 12 of the NPPF. The discharge of details is required prior to commencement of development as there may be parts of the existing buildings that need to be recorded/collated prior to demolition.
Condition : 10 - Details of Materials (condition 4 PP 2017/1847)
Prior to the commencement of each relevant building between Numbers 1 to 9 Church Row, details of the materials listed below to be used in the historic buildings shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority prior to commencement of the relevant works. The works shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details, excluding repair work listed in Condition 3. 
a)	All new materials and fixtures and fittings relating to new works to and/or in close proximity (extensions) to the historic external fabric.
b)	Replacement brick where applicable
c)	Paint finishes to new work
d)	Stone
e)	New cast iron railings and grilles
f)	Brick bond
g)	New tile (extension)
h)	Reclaimed brick (extension)
i)	New windows (extension)
j)	Internal - all new materials and fixtures and fittings relating to new works to the interiors, including fire protection measures.

Reason: In order to assess the suitability of the proposed materials and works, in the interests of the appearance of the locality, in accordance with Council policy DMS1 and DMS2. It is necessary for the condition to be discharged prior to the commencement of works to ensure suitable materials are used in the proposal and do not harm heritage assets.
Condition : 11 - Motion sensors during construction (condition 6 PP 2017/1847)
Motion sensors shall to be fitted to the retained buildings on site to monitor movement during construction on site. The findings of the monitoring shall be submitted to the local planning authority prior to occupation of any part of the development.
Reason: In order to protect the historic buildings in accordance with Council policy DMS2.
Condition : 12 - Protective measures during demolition (condition 7 PP 2017/1847)
Protective measures during demolition works on site, especially for the brick passages through 1-6 Church Row and for the retained interiors, shall be submitted to the local planning authority for approval prior to commencement of development of works which concern the listed buildings excluding demolition. Works shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved measures.

Reason: In order to protect the historic buildings in accordance with Council policy DMS2. It is necessary for this condition to be discharged prior to commencement of works to ensure that no harm is caused to heritage assets on site during construction.
Condition : 13 - Details of ventilation (condition 8 PP 2017/1847)
Prior to the commencement of each relevant building between Numbers 1 to 9 Church Row, details of ventilation for proposed bathrooms and kitchens and how any historic panelling/fabric will be protected shall be submitted to the local planning authority for approval in writing prior to those works being undertaken. Works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

Reason: In order to protect the historic buildings in accordance with Council policy DMS2.
Condition : 14 - The developer shall give the local planning authority [28] days advance written notice of the start of any works and, for a period of [14] days before any work begins, reasonable access to the building(s) shall be given to the Assistant Director of Planning and Transport and/or a body nominated by the local planning authority for the purpose of recording the building(s) and interior(s) by making measured drawings and or taking photographs  
Reason: To ensure the preservation of the special interest of the building affected by the works hereby approved, in accordance with policy LP3 of the Local Plan coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework.
Condition : 15 - INFORMATIVE: In dealing with this application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive manner and the Council has, as far as practicable, sought solutions to problems arising in relation to dealing with the planning application. The Council has made available detailed advice in the form of its statutory policies in the Local Plan (2023) as well as offering a full pre-application advice service, in order to ensure that the applicant has been given every opportunity to submit an application which is likely to be considered favourably. In addition, where appropriate, further guidance was offered to the applicant during the processing of the application.
Condition : 16 - INFORMATIVE: Written schemes of investigation will need to be prepared and implemented by a suitably qualified archaeological practice in accordance with Historic England Greater London Archaeology guidelines.  They must be approved by the local planning authority before any on-site development related activity occurs.
